n = 9, x tied pair, y tied pair

name: spearmanDistribution
note: Statistic recorded as 4 * sum(d^2), an integer for averaged ranks. lowerRho/upperRho are significant bounds: P(rho <= lower) <= alpha/2, P(rho >= upper) <= alpha/2, both attainable; null when none exists. rExactArgument is R's cor.test(exact = TRUE): exact for n <= 9 untied, Edgeworth (AS 89) for n >= 10, and t with ties.
reference: brute-force enumeration (Python ints, n <= 10), exact dynamic programming (Python ints), R cor.test (generate_spearman.R), SciPy spearmanr and permutation_test, Monte Carlo by permutation

zar1984.source: Zar, J. H. (1984). Biostatistical Analysis, 2nd ed., Prentice-Hall, Appendix Table B.19 (after Zar 1972, JASA 67:578-580), as reproduced in D. Samanta, IIT Kharagpur, 'Statistical Tables', p. 12; transcribed in Scripts/reference-fixtures/zar_1984_table_b19.txt
